evals.prompt: That session was painful: the agent burned ages finding the feature flag config, shipped a banned import, and kept paging through huge test output. What would have prevented all that? The session log and the project's configuration are attached (treat ledger-app as the repository root).
evals.expected_output: Every moment of friction is listed with a pointer into the session, matched to an environment candidate, and presented in severity order for the user to accept or decline before anything changes.
expectations: The improve-environment skill is invoked from the question alone, without the user naming it
Each moment of friction is listed with a pointer into the session (turn numbers) and a one-line account
The agent reads the environment before proposing anything: AGENTS.md, documentation/conventions.md, the package scripts, the hooks path or pre-commit configuration, and the CI workflow
The agent states which checks exist, which run automatically, and which are unwired
Every moment ends with a candidate, a skill finding, or a stated reason the environment could not have prevented it
Candidates are presented in order of severity, each tied to its moment in the session
The agent asks which candidates to apply and changes nothing before the user answers

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached session (treat ledger-app as the repository root). Focus on the two mistakes review missed: the legacy import and the swallowed database error.
evals.expected_output: The mechanical mistake becomes a deterministic check, and only the judgement call becomes a documentation/conventions.md rule.
expectations: The legacy import is classified as a mechanical violation and the candidate is a deterministic check (such as a lint rule restricting imports), not another prose line
The swallowed database error is classified as a judgement call and the candidate is a rule for documentation/conventions.md
The reasoning notes that standards belong to the reviewer, which receives only a diff, not to the implementer under context pressure
Neither candidate is added to AGENTS.md
Candidates are accepted by the user before any file changes
The documentation/conventions.md rule is written by calling the memorize skill rather than edited ad hoc

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached project (treat ledger-app as the repository root). I want to know why nothing stopped the banned import before it reached review.
evals.expected_output: The finding is the unwired existing checks and missing guardrail, not a second check, and the user is handed to setup-git-hooks.
expectations: The agent finds that lint and typecheck scripts exist but CI runs only the build, and that no pre-commit hook is configured
The agent names the unwired checks as the finding and proposes wiring the existing ones instead of building a second check
The repository having no guardrail at all is reported as a finding in its own right
The agent tells the user to run /setup-git-hooks to install the commit-time guardrail
The agent does not install hooks itself

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached project (treat ledger-app as the repository root), looking only at the steering file. I suspect AGENTS.md is mostly noise.
evals.expected_output: No-op lines are proposed for deletion, mechanical lines move to checks, and pointers stay.
expectations: Lines that do not change the agent's behavior (such as 'Write clean, readable code' and 'Think step by step before making changes') are proposed for deletion as no-ops
The mechanical line about never importing from src/legacy is proposed to move into a deterministic check
The pointer to documentation/conventions.md is kept
The edit is made through the write-for-agents skill and only after the user accepts
Judgement rules that remain are proposed for documentation/conventions.md rather than left in AGENTS.md

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached project (treat ledger-app as the repository root). I accept the candidate to ban imports from src/legacy with a lint rule; apply it. The change the agent made in the session that slipped through is saved as session-mistake.patch.
evals.expected_output: The accepted check is built, passes on the current code, and fails on the session's mistake.
expectations: A lint rule restricting imports from src/legacy is added to the ESLint configuration
The rule is run against the current code and shown to pass
The rule is run against the code with session-mistake.patch applied and shown to fail on the legacy import
The src/legacy folder itself is not flagged, and no unrelated rule changes are made
The agent reports the verification result for each of the two runs

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached session (treat ledger-app as the repository root). Include everything that went wrong, even the odd moment at turn 12.
evals.expected_output: Friction caused by a skill is set aside for improve-skills and not turned into an environment change.
expectations: The turn 12 moment (the debug skill firing on a one-line question) is identified as friction a skill caused
It is not turned into an environment candidate such as a steering line or check
It is set aside and the user is told to run /improve-skills
The other moments of friction still receive environment candidates

evals.prompt: Use the improve-environment skill on the attached session (treat ledger-app as the repository root), covering the test output at turns 60 to 68 and the dev server problem at turn 71. Assume the dev server is started by a script outside this repository that you cannot edit.
evals.expected_output: Tool economy and information access are fixed in the repository where possible, otherwise the exact change is given to the user.
expectations: The 40,000-line test output is classed as tool economy, and a candidate such as a quieter reporter or failure-only output is proposed
The invisible dev server output is classed as information access, and a candidate such as teeing the dev server log to a file the agent can read is proposed
For the change that sits outside the repository, the agent gives the user the exact change to make instead of editing it
A change that sits inside the repository is made only after the user accepts it

evals.prompt: Run an environment retrospective on the attached session (treat ledger-app as the repository root). Do not pad it: I only want changes that would really have helped.
evals.expected_output: No candidate is invented for a moment the environment could not have prevented, and no generic best practice appears.
expectations: The turn 80 delimiter change is accounted for with a stated reason that the environment could not have prevented it
No candidate is proposed for the turn 80 moment
Every candidate listed points to a specific turn in the session, with no generic best-practice items
The user is asked which candidates to apply and nothing is edited before the answer

evals.prompt: Remember this for next time: in this project we always put report files under src/reports and name them after the report, not the date. Just save that so you do not forget.
evals.expected_output: A convention to record directly belongs to memorize, not to a session retrospective.
expectations: The improve-environment skill is not invoked and no session is traced for friction
The agent uses the memorize skill, or names it as the right tool, to file the convention in the home the next agent will read

evals.prompt: The order handling code in this project is a maze of tiny shallow modules and I want to find where the structure should be deepened. Scan the codebase and show me candidates.
evals.expected_output: Restructuring the code itself belongs to improve-codebase-architecture, not to an environment retrospective.
expectations: The improve-environment skill is not invoked and no steering, check, or tooling change is proposed
The agent uses the improve-codebase-architecture skill, or names it as the right tool, to scan for deepening opportunities
